sentences.text: Author: Pankaj Purohit Bench: Pankaj Purohit

Office Notes, reports, orders or SL. proceedings or directions and  Date COURT'S OR No Registrar's order with  Signatures  WPCRL No.1359 of 2025  Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Sagar Kothari, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Rakesh Negi, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. Mr. Pavan Kumar Nath, learned counsel for the respondent no.4-informant.
4.

By means of present writ petition, petitioner has put to challenge the FIR No.0157 of 2025 dated 24.09.2025, under Section 120-B, 420, 464, 468, 471, 504 & 506 IPC, registered with Police Station Cantt, District Dehradun and other ancillary relief for not arresting the petitioner in connection with the aforesaid FIR.
5.

The first information report was lodged by respondent no. 4 (informant) against various persons,
including the petitioner, Gagan Sehgal.

It was stated therein that the property in dispute had been agreed to be sold by its owner to respondent no. 4 through an agreement of sale, and that a sale consideration of Rs.68 lakhs had been paid by respondent no. 4 to Neetu Srivastava, the owner of the property.
In the FIR, the informant alleged that a criminal conspiracy was hatched by various persons to grab the property.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner's wife, Garima Sehgal, had purchased the property in question from Radha, Anil Kumar, Neelam Narang, Ashok Kumar, Annu Arora, and Beena Rani through their power of attorney holder, Neetu Srivastava, by way of a registered sale deed for a consideration of Rs.35 lakhs, and that she is in possession of the said property.
7.
Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that there is no allegation in the FIR against the petitioner regarding cheating or forgery.

He also argued that respondent no. 4 did not acquire any rights over the property in question pursuant to the execution of an unregistered agreement to WPCRL/1359/2025 on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23529099/
1 sell.
It was further submitted that the petitioner is a bona fide purchaser of the property from its true owner, and that no criminality is attached to him in respect of the present FIR.
8. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent no. 4 submitted that he had executed an unregistered agreement to sell and had paid Rs.68 lakhs as full consideration for the said property.
He further stated that possession was handed over to him, yet the same property was subsequently executed by Neetu Srivastava and Rajeev Srivastava in favour of the petitioner.

9. Having considered the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, this Court is of the view that, prima facie, no criminality can be attributed to the petitioner at this stage, as he appears to be a bona fide purchaser of the property.
10. Learned counsel for the respondents prays for and is granted six weeks' time to file counter affidavit.
Till the next date of listing, it is directed that no coercive measures shall be taken against the petitioner, pursuant to the impugned FIR, provided he cooperates with the investigation.
13. Stay application (IA No.1/2025) stands disposed of accordingly.

(Pankaj Purohit, J.) 06.11.2025 AK WPCRL/1359/2025 on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23529099/
